cards.name: Percentage Counter Monospaced
cards.summary: Turns the text layer into an animated percentage readout that counts from 0% to 100%; every digit sits in a fixed-width slot, so the number does not jitter as it counts.
use_for: Stat reveal in an explainer ('turnout rose to 67%')
Poll or survey result callouts in news reels
Progress / completion meter next to a bar or ring
Budget share or growth-rate figures in documentaries
avoid: Pad Zeros defaults to 3, so small values read '007%' while counting: set Pad Zeros to 1
It replaces the layer's Source Text with an expression-driven counter, so typed text is lost (the layer's own font was kept in the test render: check the style after applying)
Number Format offers only 1,234,567.01 / 1.234.567,01 / 1 234 567,01 grouping: no Indian lakh/crore style (12,34,567)
Default keys end at 100: change the second Animate Value key for other targets
cards.duration_note: Animate Value is keyframed 0 -> 100 from comp.time to comp.time + 1.2 s, then holds. The Source Text and selector expressions run for the whole layer.
cards.scripting: Needs a text layer (its Source Text is replaced: an expression builds the digit template from the preset's stored text style, and Character Offset animators set each digit). Set comp.time, select only that text layer, then layer.applyPreset(new File(<batch 'file' path>)). Adds the pseudo effect 'Percentage Counter Controls' (match name 'Pseudo/ADBE Percentage Controls') with: Animate Value (keyed 0->100), 10x Value Multiplier (1 = x1; each +1 multiplies by 10), Pad Zeros (3), Digits After Decimal (0), Number Format popup (1 '1,234,567.01' en-US = default, 2 '1.234.567,01' de-DE, 3 '1 234 567,01' fr-FR), Percent Symbol Position (point), Percent Symbol Scale (100), Show Group Separators (off), Group Spacing, Group Separator Offset, Align Group Spacing popup (1 Left, 2 Right, 3 Center = default). Retarget: fx = layer.property('Effects').property('Pseudo/ADBE Percentage Controls'); fx.property('Animate Value').setValueAtKey(2, 67); move keys with setValueAtTime/removeKey to change speed. The instance name is stored with a leading tab ('\tPercentage Counter Controls'), so look it up by match name, not display name. To restyle: var d = layer.property('Source Text').value; d.font = '<PostScript name>'; layer.property('Source Text').setValue(d). Expressions need the JavaScript engine (project default).

verified.note: Counter reads 027% at 0.5 s and 098% at 1.4 s, reaching 100% at about 1.5 s; digits stay in fixed slots with Pad Zeros 3, and the layer kept its Bebas Neue font.
verified.second_opinion: agree: 474a/474b read 027% and 098% in the condensed Bebas Neue of the layer, not Myriad Pro, so the avoid[1] fix is right.

cards.name: Timer Countdown Monospaced
cards.summary: Turns the text layer into a digital countdown clock (HH : MM : SS by default, with 'Hour Mins Secs' labels on a second line); digits sit in fixed-width slots so they do not jump as they tick. Animate Value is in the largest unit of the format (hours for HH:MM:SS), so the default keys race from 09 : 59 : 59 to 00 : 00 : 00 in 1.6 s.
use_for: Countdown to a vote, result or launch in news reels
'Time left' urgency card in social reels
Clock overlay for a timeline segment (rescue operation, deadline)
avoid: Labels are fixed English words ('Hour Mins Secs'): switch Show Labels off for Hindi copy
Default keys run Animate Value 10 -> 0 (ten HOURS of clock) in 1.6 s: re-key it for a real-time countdown
Sets the layer's Source Text (expression plus the preset's Montserrat SemiBold style; substituted if the font is missing)
cards.duration_note: Animate Value is keyframed 9.9999 -> 0 (eased) from comp.time to comp.time + 1.6 s, then holds at zero: the clock shows 09 : 59 : 59 counting to 00 : 00 : 00. The clock expressions run for the whole layer.
cards.scripting: Needs a text layer (Source Text is replaced by an expression that builds the clock template with the preset's stored Montserrat SemiBold style; Character Offset animators set the digits). Set comp.time, select only that text layer, then layer.applyPreset(new File(<batch 'file' path>)). Adds the pseudo effect 'Timer Countdown Controls' (match name 'Pseudo/ADBE Timer Controls') with: Animate Value (keyed ~10->0), Time Format popup (1 MM:SS, 2 HH:MM:SS = default, 3 DD:HH:MM:SS), Show Labels (on), Label Position Offset (point), Label Size (32), Label Spacing, Separator Character popup (1 Colons = default, 2 Dots, 3 Spaces), Spacing. Unit of Animate Value (read from the digit expressions): its integer part is the FIRST field and the fraction fills the rest, i.e. hours in HH:MM:SS, minutes in MM:SS, days in DD:HH:MM:SS. Real-time N-second countdown: HH:MM:SS -> keys N/3600 at start and 0 at start + N s; MM:SS -> N/60 and 0; set both keys to KeyframeInterpolationType.LINEAR (the preset's keys are eased). fx = layer.property('Effects').property('Pseudo/ADBE Timer Controls') (the instance name is stored with a leading tab, so prefer the match name). Expressions need the JavaScript engine (project default).

verified.note: A digital clock with HOUR MINS SECS labels counts down 08:31:52 (0.5 s) to 02:23:56 (1.4 s) in fixed-width digits.

cards.name: Autumn
cards.summary: The whole line falls about 300 px down into place from above, swaying side to side and skewing like a falling leaf, settling after 2.4 s (about 2.9 s in a 25 fps comp) with a fixed 10-degree skew (faux italic).
use_for: Soft title entrance for nature or seasonal documentary segments
Calm lower-third drift-in for interview pieces
Chapter title for reflective or nostalgic sections
avoid: No fade: the text starts at full opacity 300 px above its spot; in the 960x540 test a centred title was almost entirely off the top edge at the first frame (only its bottom few pixels showed), so mask, fade or plan for it dropping in from off-frame
Ends skewed 10 degrees (Skew expression is cos(y/20)*10, which is 10 at rest): change it to Math.sin(n/20)*10 to end upright
Too whimsical for hard news or political attack copy
cards.duration_note: Animator Position is keyed from 300 px above (negative Y) to 0 between comp.time and comp.time + 2.4 s at 30 fps (about 2.9 s in a 25 fps comp, since the keys keep their frame counts); the sway/skew expressions follow that motion and stop when it lands.
cards.scripting: Needs a text layer. Set comp.time to the start second, open the comp (comp.openInViewer()), select only the target text layer, then layer.applyPreset(new File(<batch 'file' path>)). Your Source Text is kept; the preset adds text animators. The side-to-side sway and skew are expressions driven by the Position keyframes (sin/cos of the Y offset). Expressions need the JavaScript engine (project default).

verified.note: The line high above its spot at 0.5 s and still falling, about 60 px above it, at 1.4 s, with an italic skew.
verified.recheck: 2026-10-13: re-rendered in live wave 1 (frames the old verdict was judged on: pve/work/gallery_pre_fix/)

cards.summary: Replaces the text with 'Balance' on a small mask path; the per-word Grouping Alignment is keyed left and right (0 -> -40 -> 80 -> -80 -> 40 -> 0%) over about 3.9 s, so the word teeters back and forth on the curve as if balancing on a beam, then settles.
use_for: 'Balance' or trade-off concepts in explainers (budget, policy)
avoid: Replaces your text and font with the preset's own 'Balance' in Myriad Pro Condensed: save and restore the text (see scripting)
Built for one word on a short 276 px arc: long lines run off the path
cards.duration_note: Grouping-alignment keys run from comp.time to comp.time + 3.92 s and end at the start value.
cards.scripting: Needs a text layer. Set comp.time to the start second, open the comp (comp.openInViewer()), select only the target text layer, then layer.applyPreset(new File(<batch 'file' path>)). It adds a mask to the layer and sets Text > Path Options > Path to it (plus animators). The preset ALSO sets Source Text: your text is replaced by 'Balance' in Myriad Pro Condensed. Save d = layer.property('Source Text').value before applyPreset, then afterwards set nd = layer.property('Source Text').value; nd.text = d.text; nd.font = d.font; nd.fontSize = d.fontSize; layer.property('Source Text').setValue(nd) (this keeps the preset's paragraph alignment, which its Grouping Alignment keys expect). The mask is drawn in layer space around the text origin, about 276 x 138 px (small in 1920x1080); scale or move it via layer.property('Masks').property(1).property('Mask Path') or scale the layer. Keyed property (read from the file): Text > More Options > Grouping Alignment, with Anchor Point Grouping = Word; the teeter look itself is inferred, verify on a test render.

verified.note: Balance sits tilted on its path at 0.5 s and level at 1.4 s, teetering as described.
